title: CPlane radar handovers - standup notes 2026-06-30
content:
Meeting: Control Plane - Radar & Handover Standup
Date: 2026-06-30 10:00am PDT (30m) — quick sync before July sprint kickoff
Attendees: Aisha, Miguel, Priya, Liam, Zara, Ravi (joined for routing block)

Purpose: quick cross-functional visibility across control plane, routing edges, auth token flow, and quota enforcement ahead of next-week canary. Focus is on handoffs, outstanding blockers, and short action items rather than long design reviews.

1) High-level summary
- Control plane is stable; no active P0s.
- Routing team seeing intermittent 5xx spikes on EU edge during high-concurrency tests (see PLAT-4328).
- Auth refresh latency spiked last night after the library bump; rollback applied to staging while we investigate (AUTH-211).
- Quotas subsystem has a pending change to quota key sharding for per-customer throttles — planned for canary next Tuesday.

2) Control plane updates (Aisha)
- Completed rollout of API server autoscaler config (canary at 10% traffic). Observed expected CPU downshift and stable token bucket behavior. No errors so far.
- Work in progress: apply additional tracing tags for routing decisions to link request -> route policy evaluation (instrumentation ticket PLAT-4335, not yet in Jira).
- Action: add a short note to Confluence about autoscaler knobs and expected impact on KV cache thrash (Aisha, due 2026-07-02).

3) Routing & Edge (Ravi / Miguel)
- Miguel: reproduced 5xx spikes in EU during synthetic burst tests run at 03:00am UTC. Root cause preliminary: a race in the route cache refresh + connection churn when a backend variant evicts.
- Temporary mitigation: increase route cache TTL from 2s -> 8s in EU pool (will reduce churn but may delay rollouts). Deployed as hotfix to EU canary.
- Investigation next steps: add delta-logging when route cache misses coincide with LB reconnects (PLAT-4328). Priority: high for next 48 hours.
- Handovers: Miguel to hand routing runbook updates to SRE on-call with explicit rollback steps if increased TTL causes stale routing tests to fail. (Miguel -> SRE docs, due 2026-07-01)

4) Auth (Priya)
- After library bump to oauth-client v3.2.0, we saw a 12% uplift in token refresh latency for refresh flows which bubbled into tail latencies for some short-lived sessions. Quick rollback to v3.1.7 on staging and rollforward blocked for now.
- Reproduction steps captured in AUTH-211; Priya attached traces to the Jira ticket.
- Action: run focused perf suite on oauth-client (Priya + Liam) to isolate whether the regression is in the client or upstream KMS interaction. Scheduled slot: 2026-07-01 09:30am.

5) Quotas (Zara)
- Quota key sharding: prototype validated on a subset of customers; 0.6% error delta observed in synthetic tests. Need canary with real traffic to confirm correctness under production variance.
- Risk: if sharding misaligns with existing caching layers, we risk overcounting during merges. To reduce risk, will enable sharding behind feature flag and apply to 5% of customers during canary.
- Action: Zara to prepare rollout checklist and add a backwards-compatibility test to the acceptance suite (due 2026-07-05).

6) Cross-team coordination items
- Canary window: proposed Tuesday 2026-07-06 from 02:00–06:00 UTC for quotas sharding + route-cache TTL update. Need SRE presence and quick rollback playbooks for both subsystems.
- Observability: add a composite dashboard that correlates route-cache misses, auth refresh latency, and quota enforcement rejects for the canary. Miguel + Priya to draft panel list by EOD 2026-07-01.
- Backpressure test: run end-to-end test that simulates short-lived token churn + routing variant roll (Liam to script; target run: 2026-07-02).

7) Blockers and escalations
- Blocker: flaky end-to-end test used to validate quotas is returning nondeterministic results on CI (flaky tier-2). Investigation points to time-based test ordering — patch pending. Owner: Zara. Impact: delays canary certs by 48 hours if not fixed.
- Escalation: request from SRE to pause any further client library bumps until auth perf regression is fully stabilized (SRE request logged in AUTH-211).

8) Decisions made in this standup
- Increase route cache TTL in EU pool to 8s as temporary mitigation (accepting longer rollout propagation time).
- Pause oauth-client rollforward until perf regression root cause is identified.
- Proceed with quotas sharding canary behind feature flag and limited to 5% traffic.

9) Action items (owners and due dates)
- Miguel: update routing runbook + add TTL hotfix rollback steps (due 2026-07-01).
- Priya: run oauth-client perf suite and attach full flamegraphs to AUTH-211 (due 2026-07-01).
- Liam: build backpressure E2E script simulating token churn + route variant roll (due 2026-07-02).
- Zara: fix flaky quota acceptance test and add BC case, prepare canary checklist (due 2026-07-05).
- Aisha: Confluence note on autoscaler tuning and KV cache expectations (due 2026-07-02).

10) Quick notes / working ideas (brainstorm fragments)
- Consider adding a short-lived intermediate route-cache tier keyed by backend variant fingerprint so we can reduce simultaneous evictions during rollouts. Pros/cons TBD.
- Explore optimistic quota merging with delayed reconciliation instead of synchronous merges for large customers — could reduce hot-path latency but complicates accounting.
- Add a small experiment to the canary to test increasing auth token TTL by 10% for short-lived sessions to reduce refresh pressure; measure customer-visible latency impact.

11) Handover checklist for on-call (short bullet cheatsheet)
- If EU 5xx spike shows up: revert route cache TTL to 2s, escalate to Miguel, enable increased logging, do not change quotas during window.
- If auth refresh tail > 200ms: toggle oauth-client to v3.1.7, open AUTH-211 and tag SRE lead.
- If quota enforcement rejects jump by >2%: roll feature flag back for quotas sharding, run reconciliation job, contact Zara.

Next meeting: 2026-07-02 10:00am PDT — quick sync before canary.

Notes: this doc is intentionally a concise operational snapshot for handovers. Longer design proposals and postmortem follow-ups will live on Confluence (linked above). Please add comments inline or ping me on Slack if you want any changes to the runbook text before I publish the final version.
